_metadata.task: TCGA BRCA IDC versus ILC subtype classification
_metadata.source: Subtype-specific descriptions derived from the checked-in MAPLE BRCA attribute bank

small_mag: Invasive ductal carcinoma shows cohesive irregular glands, ducts, solid nests, or cords infiltrating breast stroma.
The tumor-stroma interface is often irregular and accompanied by a prominent desmoplastic fibrotic response.
Low-power architecture is heterogeneous, with variable tubule formation, solid growth, and occasional necrosis.
Tumor cells commonly form cohesive nests and clusters rather than single-file infiltrates.
Residual ductal structures may be distorted or replaced by invasive gland-forming carcinoma.
The invasive front can be poorly circumscribed, with angular glands extending into adipose or fibrous tissue.
Dense collagenous stroma frequently separates and surrounds malignant epithelial aggregates.
Areas of increased cellularity alternate with glandular regions and fibrotic stroma across the slide.
Tumor-associated inflammation and stromal remodeling may be conspicuous around invasive nests.
Overall low-resolution appearance favors a cohesive duct-forming carcinoma with desmoplastic invasion.
big_mag: Invasive ductal carcinoma contains cohesive atypical epithelial cells with recognizable cell-cell adhesion.
Irregular tubules or glands are lined by malignant cells with enlarged pleomorphic nuclei.
Nucleoli may be prominent and mitotic figures may be present within cellular tumor regions.
Cell borders are generally more cohesive than in lobular carcinoma, producing compact nests and glands.
Luminal differentiation can be seen as small glandular spaces or duct-like structures.
Nuclear size and shape are variable, with hyperchromasia and loss of normal epithelial polarity.
Dense desmoplastic collagen is often directly apposed to malignant glands or solid epithelial clusters.
Necrotic debris or apoptotic material may occur within poorly formed glandular lumina.
Tumor cells can display moderate eosinophilic cytoplasm and irregular nuclear membranes.
High-resolution morphology favors cohesive malignant epithelial proliferation with ductal or glandular differentiation.

small_mag: Invasive lobular carcinoma shows diffuse, poorly circumscribed infiltration through otherwise preserved breast architecture.
Tumor cells spread as thin linear cords and single-file arrays through collagenous stroma.
A targetoid pattern may be present as malignant cells concentrically surround benign ducts and lobules.
Low-power tumor density can be deceptively low because cells infiltrate individually rather than forming a mass.
The stromal reaction is often less bulky than the desmoplasia surrounding invasive ductal carcinoma.
Normal structures may remain recognizable despite widespread permeation by small discohesive tumor cells.
Linear Indian-file infiltration creates subtle parallel tracks between collagen bundles.
The invasive boundary is indistinct, with diffuse extension beyond the apparent main tumor area.
Solid gland-forming nests and well-developed tubules are generally absent at low magnification.
Overall low-resolution appearance favors a diffuse discohesive carcinoma preserving background tissue contours.
big_mag: Invasive lobular carcinoma contains small discohesive malignant cells infiltrating in single-file arrangements.
Loss of cell-cell cohesion produces isolated cells and loose linear cords without true gland formation.
Nuclei are often round to oval and relatively uniform, with inconspicuous nucleoli in classic areas.
Scant cytoplasm and subtle atypia can make individual infiltrating cells difficult to recognize.
Signet-ring morphology may occur when intracytoplasmic mucin displaces the nucleus eccentrically.
Tumor cells may encircle ducts in a targetoid pattern while leaving the duct epithelium intact.
Indian-file cords pass between collagen fibers with minimal disruption of the extracellular matrix.
Cell borders are indistinct and cohesive nests are uncommon compared with invasive ductal carcinoma.
Tubule and lumen formation are absent or very limited in classic invasive lobular carcinoma.
High-resolution morphology favors monotonous discohesive cells with single-file stromal infiltration.
